title: Orbán Relaunches Fidesz Opposition Strategy at Annual Kötcse Speech, Threatens NVVH Staff
detail: Viktor Orbán delivered Fidesz's traditional closed-door season-opening speech at Kötcse on September 12 — his first since losing power in April — outlining a strategy to rebuild the party from opposition. Orbán cast himself as leading the political offensive while assigning deputy Fidesz chair János Bóka a defensive brief, urged the fragmented Hungarian right to stay unified rather than splinter (a swipe at the breakaway 'Democratic Citizens' initiative led by Tibor Navracsics and Csaba Ferencz), and argued Fidesz should stop re-litigating its April defeat and instead attack the Magyar government's record. He accused the Tisza government of turning Hungary into a 'Brussels colony' by surrendering economic sovereignty, and framed the planned 2030 euro adoption as cover for austerity. Details of the closed speech emerged through leaks to Hungarian media rather than an official transcript.

media.caption: Viktor Orbán at Fidesz's annual Kötcse gathering, outlining a strategy to return to power

title: Orbán Threatens Anti-Corruption Office Staff With 'Accountability' If Fidesz Returns to Power
detail: In a September 13 interview with Zsolt Bayer on HírTV following his Kötcse speech, Viktor Orbán warned employees of the new anti-corruption and asset-recovery agency NVVH that if Fidesz regains office, their names would be made public and they would face 'financial and legal accountability,' comparing the agency to the communist-era secret police (ÁVH). The remark, aimed at an institution created specifically to investigate alleged Orbán-era state asset misappropriation, was widely read in Hungarian media as an explicit intimidation threat against civil servants and drew condemnation from Tisza and rule-of-law commentators as an attempt to deter NVVH staff from pursuing politically sensitive cases.

media.caption: Orbán tells Zsolt Bayer that NVVH staff will face 'accountability' if Fidesz returns to power
